Package com.signalwire.sdk.relay

Enum Class DialState

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<DialState>
com.signalwire.sdk.relay.DialState
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<DialState>, Constable
public enum DialState extends Enum<DialState>
The outcome state of an outbound calling.dial, as a typed, compile-time-checked closed set.

A dial progresses dialing → answered (a leg won) or dialing → failed (every leg gave up). The RELAY server reports it as the bare dial_state field on each calling.call.dial event. This enum mirrors the three values the Java port declares in Constants as DIAL_STATE_* (Constants.DIAL_STATE_DIALING / Constants.DIAL_STATE_ANSWERED / Constants.DIAL_STATE_FAILED), which back the dial-completion logic in RelayClient.handleDialEvent.

It is exposed alongside the existing string getter, never instead of it: RelayEvent.CallDialEvent.getDialState() keeps returning the raw wire string (parity with Python, forward-compatible), while RelayEvent.CallDialEvent.getDialStateEnum() returns Optional<DialState> for callers who want a typed handle and an isTerminal() predicate.

Terminal semantics. Unlike CallState (where only ended is terminal), both ANSWERED and FAILED are terminal dial outcomes — each resolves the pending dial (one completes the CompletableFuture<Call>, the other fails it). Only DIALING is non-terminal. So "terminal" here means "the dial has a final outcome", matching the answered/failed branches that resolve the dial in RelayClient. 


 event.getDialState();                       // "answered" (always present, parity)
 event.getDialStateEnum()
      .filter(DialState::isTerminal)          // ANSWERED or FAILED
      .ifPresent(s -> ...);

Server-emitted, growable — fromWire(String) returns null for an unrecognised value rather than throwing (the Java analog of Rust's #[non_exhaustive] + fallible from_str); an unknown dial state must never crash event dispatch.

This is a DISTINCT vocabulary from CallState and MessageState. A dial outcome (dialing/answered/failed) is not a call lifecycle state and not a message delivery state. Note in particular answered appears in both DialState and CallState but means different things (the dial won vs. the call leg is up) — the two enums are never shared.

    • isTerminal

      public boolean isTerminal()
      Whether this is a terminal dial outcome — i.e. the dial has a final result and will not transition further. Both ANSWERED and FAILED are terminal (each resolves the pending dial); only DIALING is non-terminal.
      Returns:
      true iff this state is ANSWERED or FAILED.

    • fromWire

      public static DialState fromWire(String wire)
      Parse a wire string into a DialState, or return null if it is not one of the three recognised dial states. Because the set mirrors server-emitted values that may grow, an unknown string is tolerated (returns null) rather than rejected with an exception.

      wire - the candidate wire string (case-sensitive), may be null.

      the matching constant, or null if none matches.
